Satyen Vaidya, Judge Petitioner is an accused of offences under Sections 363, 376 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 6 of the Protection 1 Whether reporters of the local papers may be allowed to see the judgment?
Neutral Citation No. ( 2024:HHC:6967 ) of Children from Sexual Offence, Act (for short "POCSO Act") and is facing trial for said offences before learned Special Judge (I), Kullu, in Sessions Trial No. 6 of 2022.

2. FIR bearing No. 18 of 2022, dated 01.02.2022, was registered at Police Station Bhuntar, District Kullu, H.P. at the instance of mother of the victim alleging inter alia that the victim was suspected to have been kidnapped by the petitioner.
The victim was alleged to be a student of 9th Class and aged about 14 years.
3. The police allegedly recovered the victim on 01.02.2022 from the house of the sister of the petitioner.
During investigation, on the basis of the statement of the victim, Sections 376 and 506 of the IPC and Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, were added.
The victim complained of having been repeatedly assaulted sexually by petitioner at different places between 19.01.2022 to 31.01.2022.
4. On completion of investigation, report under Section 173(2) of the Code of Criminal Neutral Citation No. ( 2024:HHC:6967 ) Procedure, was submitted.

sentences.text: Consequently, petitioner is facing the trial as noticed above.
Eleven prosecution witnesses including the victim and her mother have already been examined in the trial.

5. The prayer for bail has been made on the grounds firstly, that the implication of the petitioner is false and is on account of enmity between the mother of victim and the family of the petitioner,
secondly, the medical evidence does not support the prosecution case and lastly, the trial of the petitioner has been unduly delayed whereby his constitutional right to speedy trial has been infringed.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the petitioner as well as learned Deputy Advocate General and have also gone through the status report.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioner in addition to the above mentioned grounds raised for grant of bail, submitted that the petitioner is permanent resident of Village Pasha, P.O. Kalath, Neutral Citation No. ( 2024:HHC:6967 ) Tehsil Manali, District Kullu, H.P.
No criminal history has been attached to the petitioner.
Petitioner being a local resident of the State of Himachal Pradesh and having roots in society is not likely to abscond from the course of justice.

It has further been submitted that all material witnesses have already been examined and therefore, there is no likelihood of adverse effect on the remaining trial, by release of petitioner on bail.
8.

On the other hand, learned Deputy Advocate General, has opposed the bail petition by alleging that the petitioner has been charged with very serious and heinous offence and he does not deserve liberty of bail.

It is submitted that the petitioner is a threat to the society and in case he is released on bail not only there is an apprehension of his indulging in similar activities, he may also flee from the course of justice with a purpose to avoid punishment.
9. Petitioner is in custody in the present case since 01.12.2022.
Almost thirty months have Neutral Citation No. ( 2024:HHC:6967 ) elapsed thereafter, but the trial against petitioner is not likely to conclude in near future.
This Court has been informed that the first prosecution witness was examined during trial on 25.02.2023 and the last being eleventh prosecution witness was examined on 27.03.2024.
Nine more witnesses of prosecution are yet to be examined.
After 27.03.2024, the trial was adjourned to 03.08.2024 but no witness was examined on said date and now the trial has further been adjourned to 07.12.2024.
10. It is not a case, where the trial has been delayed for reasons attributable to the petitioner.

11. The right to speedy trial is one of the various manifestations of Article 21 of the Constitution of India and has repeatedly been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court to be a valuable right available to a person or accused of an offence.

In Dr. Vinod Bhandari Vs. State of M.P. 2015(1) Criminal Court Cases 294 (S.C.), Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as under:-
Neutral Citation No. ( 2024:HHC:6967 )
"12.

entities.text: Dr. Vinod Bhandari Vs. State of M.P. 2015(1) Criminal Court Cases 294 (S.C.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well settled that at pre-conviction stage, there is presumption of innocence.
The object of keeping a person in custody is to ensure his availability to face the trial and to receive the sentence that may be passed.
The detention is not supposed to be punitive or preventive.
Seriousness of the allegation or the availability of material in support thereof are not the only considerations for declining bail.

Delay in commencement and conclusion of trial is a factor to be taken into account and the accused cannot be kept in custody for indefinite period if trial is not likely to be concluded within reasonable time.

Reference may be made to decisions of this Court in Kalyan Chandra Sarkar vs. Rajesh Ranjan, (2005)2 SCC 42, State of U.P. vs. Amarmani Tripathi (2005) 8 SCC 21, State of Kerala vs. Raneef (2011) 1 SCC 784 and Sanjay Chandra vs. CBI, (2012)1 SCC Ajay Kumar vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91443627/
2 40."

13. In Criminal Appeal No. 943 of 2023 titled as Mohd Muslim @ Hussain Vs. State (NCT Neutral Citation No. ( 2024:HHC:6967 ) of Delhi), Hon'ble Supreme Court, vide its judgment dated 28.03.2023, has held as under: -
"21.

entities.text: Mohd Muslim @ Hussain Vs. State (NCT Neutral Citation No. ( 2024:HHC:6967 ) of Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Before parting, it would be important to reflect that laws which impose stringent conditions for grant of bail, may be necessary in public interest; yet, if trials are not concluded in time, the injustice wrecked on the individual is immeasurable.
Jails are overcrowded and their living conditions, more often than not, appalling.

According to the Union Home Ministry's response to Parliament, the National Crime Records Bureau had recorded that as on 31st December 2021, over 5,54,034 prisoners were lodged in jails against total capacity of 4,25,069 lakhs in the country.
Of these 122,852 were convicts; the rest 4,27,165 were under-trials.

22. The danger of unjust imprisonment, is that inmates are at risk of "prisonisation"
a term described by the Kerala High Court in A Convict Prisoner v. State21 as"a radical transformation" whereby the prisoner:
"loses his identity.
He is known by a number.
He loses personal possessions.
He has no personal relationships.

Psychological problems result from loss of freedom, status,
possessions, dignity any autonomy of personal life.
The inmate culture of prison turns out to be dreadful.
The prisoner becomes hostile by ordinary standards.

Self perception changes."
23.

There is a further danger of the prisoner turning to crime, "as crime not only turns admirable,
but the more professional the crime, more honour is paid to the criminal"22 (also see Donald Clemmer's 'The Prison Community' 20 National Crime Records Bureau, Prison Statistics in India https://ncrb.gov.in/sites/default/files/PSI- 2021/Executive_ncrb_Summary-2021.pdf 21 Neutral Citation No. ( 2024:HHC:6967 ) 1993 Cri LJ 3242 22 Working Papers - Group on Prisons & Borstals - 1966 U.K. published in 194023).

Incarceration has further deleterious effects - where the accused belongs to the weakest economic strata:
immediate loss of livelihood, and in several cases, scattering of families as well as loss of family bonds and alienation from society.

The courts therefore, have to be sensitive to these aspects (because in the event of an acquittal, the loss to the accused is irreparable), and ensure that trials - especially in cases, where special laws enact stringent provisions, are taken up and concluded speedily."

sentences.text: Petitioner is stated to be about 24 years of age.
No criminal antecedents have been attached to the petitioner.

He is permeant resident of Village Parsha, P.O. Kalath,
Tehsil Manali, District Kullu, H.P.
The apprehension expressed by respondent/State with respect to the possibility of petitioner fleeing from the course of justice appears to be without any basis.
15. Prosecution has already examined material witnesses including the victim and her mother.
Nothing substantial has been placed on record to suggest that in case of release of petitioner on bail, the further trial is likely to be adversely effected.
Neutral Citation No. ( 2024:HHC:6967 )
16. Petitioner has already suffered pre-trial incarceration of about thirty months.
It is more than settled that such incarceration cannot be punitive.
The presumption of innocence is available to the petitioner at this stage.
No fruitful purpose shall be served by prolonging the further pre-trial incarceration of petitioner for indefinite period.
17. In view of what has been observed above, I do not find it appropriate to comment on other contentions raised on behalf of the petitioner to avoid prejudice to either of the parties during trial.

18. In the given facts and circumstances of the case, the bail petition is allowed and petitioner is ordered to be released on bail in case FIR No. 18/2022, dated 01.02.2022, registered under Sections 363, 376 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012, at Police Station, Bhuntar, District Kullu, H.P.. on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/-
with one surety in the like amount to the Neutral Citation No. ( 2024:HHC:6967 ) satisfaction of learned Trial Court.

This order shall, however, be subject to the following conditions:-
i) Petitioner shall regularly attend the trial of the case before learned Trial Court and shall not cause any delay in its conclusion.
ii) Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence, in any manner,
whatsoever and shall not dissuade any person from speaking the truth in relation to the facts of the case in hand.
 iii) Petitioner shall be liable for immediate  arrest in the instant case in the  event of petitioner violating the  conditions of this bail.
(iv) Petitioner shall not leave India without permission of learned Trial Court till completion of trial.
19. Any expression of opinion herein-above shall have no bearing on the merits of the case and shall be deemed only for the purpose of disposal of this petition.
